The speaker mentioned that the Microsoft investors have not been trigger-happy and have not exhibited short term type thinking.

thesis: This episode argues that the speaker's 'Microsoft crew' has been with him for almost two decades and has not been trigger-happy, noting that some investors have consistently added over the years and have not taken his advice to unload Microsoft stock. The speaker also mentions that these investors have not been trigger-happy and have not exhibited short-term type thinking.

claims.claim: The speaker advised Microsoft employees not to hold Microsoft stock because it was a terrible idea, noting it went up 30-40% a year for a long time.
claims.quote: But I remember telling them at that time that, and I think they just thought I was some cheesy salesman saying this. But I told them that it was a terrible idea for them to be holding Microsoft stock.

claims.claim: The speaker noted that Microsoft stock went up 30-40% a year for a long time until recently, and eventually went down to under 200 billion.
claims.quote: Because all Microsoft had done until then had gone straight up, 30%, 40% a year for a long time. And the market cap, I think at the time, was over 600 billion. And eventually, I think it went all the way down to under 200 billion.

claims.claim: The speaker mentioned that from 2000 until maybe 2013 or 2014, you would have had almost no returns on Microsoft stock.
claims.quote: But even with Microsoft, from 2000, almost till maybe 2013 or 2014, you would have had almost no returns. And in fact, you would have had a rough ride because you would have gone down and then come up.

claims.claim: The speaker stated that in 2000, Microsoft was making around 10 billion a year and trading at 600 billion.
claims.quote: And that matters and works so well. So if we look at the S&P over the same period, similar story, where we again go through these periods of flatline. And so, basically, if I just go back to the Dow for a second, 65, 1965 extreme euphoria, 1981 extreme pessimism, then you again get to 1999 2000 extreme euphoria and so on and so forth.

claims.claim: The speaker mentioned that the Microsoft crew has been with him for almost a couple of decades and they have not been trigger-happy.
claims.quote: Actually, the Microsoft crew that has been with me, I think now they've been with me for almost a couple of decades. I haven't seen them exhibit any behavior that would be of the kind that you're suggesting. In the sense that I hardly ever hear from them and maybe they've forgotten their money with me who knows.

claims.claim: The speaker noted that some of the Microsoft investors have consistently added over the years and have not taken his advice to unload Microsoft.
claims.quote: In fact, some of them have consistently added over the years.
